# Returned rating sheets

Five completed copies of `../rater_sheet.md`, returned on 2026-10-09.

**These sheets were completed by AI assistants, not by people.** None names a human rater, and the
"About you" entries (names, roles, platforms used, time spent) were generated by the assistants and
describe no one; they must not be reported as rater demographics. The comparison with the reference
scores is therefore a second-reading robustness check, not human inter-rater reliability
(`../protocol.md`, "Status and known weaknesses"; the same framing as `docs/DECISION_LOG.md` D26).

| File | Code in the analysis | Assistant and version | Cells scored |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rater_sheet_evaluator_1.md` | P1 (S1 in the manuscript) | not recorded | 248 |
| `rater_sheet_evaluator_2.md` | P2 (S2) | not recorded | 248 |
| `rater_sheet_evaluator_3.md` | P3 (S3) | not recorded | 248 |
| `rater_sheet_evaluator_4.md` | P4 (S4) | not recorded | 248 |
| `rater_sheet_evaluator_5.md` | P5 (S5) | not recorded | 247 (one `?`) |

To record before submission: which assistant and version produced each sheet, the prompt used, and
whether web search was enabled. The sheets are kept as returned.

Known factual problems in the sheets, checked against `../verification_log.md`:

- all five score Bitbucket alone as if its issue tracker still existed (removed August 2026, V1);
- four of five score mandatory merge-request approval as available on GitLab Free (V5), and three
  of five do the same for Bitbucket Free (V20).

Analysis: `analysis/scripts/rater_agreement.py` -> `results/evaluation/panel_*`;
figure: `analysis/scripts/plot_rater_range.py` -> `manuscript_2/fig_raters.svg`.
